tickets.title: [Frontier] [DOC15-01] Publish the confirmed S15 spec and delivery graph
tickets.deliver: The confirmed S15 decisions, requirements, proposed architecture and complete synchronized issue graph are reviewable in one documentation PR; pending required UX authoring is an explicit separate prerequisite.
steps: Keep the 23 confirmed decisions separate from proposed engineering, runtime support and actual owner grants.
Preserve FR/NFR identifiers; connect each S15 acceptance case to scoped work and explicit prerequisites.
Track required Opus/high UX authoring as UX15-00 and block UI implementation until the handoff exists; do not substitute primary-authored design or claim it completed.
Publish the parent/sub-issues and direct dependency graph; verify remote issue bodies, labels, artifact links and local mirrors.
accept: S15-D01–D23 and S15-AC01–AC16 remain complete and consistent with the owner confirmation.
Default versus opt-in personal GitHub policy, report-only issue discovery, production holds and deferred Jod interoperability are explicit.
Every child has the workflow-required sections, a tier justification, concrete tests and real blockers; the spec parent is never ready-for-agent.
Pending required UI/UX authoring is explicitly tracked and blocks dependent tickets; no primary-authored design or completed-handoff claim is substituted.
All local links, dependency edges, coverage and remote mirrors validate; S14 remains the implemented default.
tests: Validate complete unique decision/acceptance/FR/NFR IDs and English-only additions.
Validate an acyclic graph, actual issue IDs, native parent/blocker relations and readiness labels against prerequisites.
Run git diff --check; runtime tests are unnecessary for documentation-only changes.
tickets.contract: Records S15 spec, ADR 0064, experience and delivery index; delivers no new runtime contract.
tickets.out: Runtime implementation, live tools, deployment, Jod integration and merging this PR.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [ARCH15-01] Freeze the working-VM and protected-effect feasibility contract
tickets.deliver: A reviewed feasibility matrix and versioned design contract identify the exact supported Schway surface, protected trust domains and honest limits before dependent implementation is declared ready.
steps: Audit the pinned Schway artifact through supported exports and existing packed-consumer fixtures; record exact capabilities and gaps.
Trace root/sudo, filesystem destruction, network, browser sessions, cookies, scripts and MCP paths against each human-required effect.
Specify candidate placement/transport/administration/data boundaries; distinguish prevention from recovery snapshots and local fixtures from real VM proof.
Deliver docs/contracts/s15-runtime-feasibility-v1.md and refine ADR 0064 with accepted/rejected choices and named remaining proof gates.
Create a Schway proposal/issue only for a demonstrated missing public contract; do not invent an upstream blocker.
accept: Every required VM/browser operation maps to a verified public export or an explicit gap; no Jit-owned provider/agent-loop replacement.
A guest administrator cannot be assumed isolated from a sibling process or guest-local firewall.
Root destruction versus major-change approval is explicitly resolved in the design or retained as a named owner tradeoff; no weaker guarantee is silently substituted.
The contract separates implementable logic from live activation gates and specifies how unknown websites/actions fail closed.
Closing this audit does not certify enforcement: downstream readiness requires the reviewed contract revision and its declared proof status.
tests: Reproduce the existing packed-host capability checks and record the pinned tarball hash/export evidence.
Produce an attack/operation matrix with allowed, held, denied and unproven outcomes for guest-root, browser and egress routes.
Validate referenced paths/signatures against current main and use no live credentials or paid calls.
tickets.contract: Delivers proposed s15-runtime-feasibility/v1; records exact supported Schway exports rather than assuming a new API.
tickets.out: Runtime rollout, provider refresh, real-account writes and concrete UI/UX.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [STATE15-01] Specify a non-destructive S14-to-S15 state and policy transition
tickets.deliver: A versioned transition inventory and recovery plan preserve S14/legacy data, private scopes and approvals while defining explicit S15 policy adoption.
steps: Inventory current schema/application identifiers, stores, policy generations, effect states, memory/privacy lineage and opaque native references.
Define compatible transitions and refusals for each record class, including stopped/cancelled/unknown work and lifecycle tombstones.
Specify explicit owner adoption of team scope and the personal GitHub exception; upgrades must not infer either from this spec.
Deliver docs/contracts/s15-state-transition-v1.md with schema/version plan, fixture input/output examples and rollback/backup checkpoints.
accept: The exact main/schema is recorded; no old fresh-state permission is treated as S15 erase/import authority.
Existing private claims/files/accounts remain restricted until an authorized conversion; personal GitHub permissions are never an upgrade default.
Unknown effects, consumed budget and lifecycle withdrawals cannot reset through backup/restore or transition.
The plan identifies exact migration signatures/record shapes and refusal cases before the implementing ticket is ready.
tests: Map fixtures for current S14 state, legacy service-config omission, withdrawn private sources and unknown effects to preserved/refused outcomes.
Document byte-preservation and prior-build rollback evidence required from the eventual implementation.
Read-only inventory only: do not open a live store writable, inspect secrets or run an installation migration.
tickets.contract: Delivers proposed s15-state-transition/v1, including schema and policy-version adoption; no schema is changed in this audit.
tickets.out: Applying migrations, choosing a live host or changing legacy/S14 activation.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [POLICY15-01] Enforce standing policy and exact held actions outside working agents
tickets.deliver: Authenticated owner policy permits ordinary bounded work and holds human-required actions with exact revision-bound approval; working agents cannot change their authority.
steps: Freeze the reviewed standing-policy/action contract and schema from ARCH15-01/STATE15-01 before implementation.
Implement owner-derived actor, purpose/resource/model/destination scopes, rule revisions, finite budget reservations and action receipts.
Distinguish ordinary reversible edits, default approval classes and explicitly captured standing exceptions; unknown policy matches hold.
Bind final approvals to exact pending action details and recheck policy/revocation at admission, execution and publication.
accept: Model/source/repository/memory/quoted-owner text cannot create or widen policy or approve an action.
A changed recipient/content/attachment/transaction, stale revision, expiry or revocation prevents execution.
Operating costs reserve within a finite configured ceiling; unknown costs/usage are not zero and unspecified budgets are not spending permission.
Default GitHub and optional personal rules are separate; policy changes and production approval cannot be made by the working agent.
Duplicate and interrupted effects produce one local intent or unknown/reconcile-only state, never blind remote retries.
tests: Scripted actor/spoofed-source and cross-purpose/resource/model fixtures -> allow/hold/deny as specified.
Fake-clock expiry, stale-rule/approval and revoke-before-execute races -> no effect.
Concurrent reservation/exhaustion and crash-before/after effect fixtures -> conservative usage and reconcile-only unknown.
tickets.contract: Delivers versioned standing-policy/action-approval contract and implementation conformance; old S14 commands are not silently reinterpreted.
tickets.out: Real account adapters, arbitrary website guarantees, guest provisioning and UI design.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [VM15-01] Run ordinary administration in the approved working VM
tickets.deliver: A supported execution backend performs real working-VM file/shell/admin tasks while protected authority and credentials remain outside guest control.
steps: Implement only the reviewed ARCH15-01 transport/administration boundary through public Schway backend contracts.
Bind VM identity, attempt/generation, resource ceilings, cancellation and operation receipts to current policy.
Exercise file processing, program/dependency installation, sudo/admin, Docker and ordinary service setup under the reviewed boundary.
Deny protected-state/session/control access and alternate network/effect paths; leave unproven capabilities inactive until EVID15-01.
accept: Commands execute in the named working VM, with no accidental protected-host shell fallback.
The required administration operations actually work; a read-only substitute is not reported as full administration.
Protected credentials/state/approval controls cannot be read, mounted, overwritten or reached via guest-local control changes.
Stop/revoke fences late outputs; cancellation retains capacity until settlement.
Destructive-operation limits and recovery/prevention distinctions match the reviewed contract and are disclosed.
tests: Scripted backend and runner fixtures -> correct guest identity, paths, limits and generation fences.
Malicious path/socket/mount/egress requests -> denied before protected access.
Opt-in controlled VM operations are recorded separately; fixtures alone do not certify guest-root isolation.
tickets.contract: Delivers the reviewed VM backend/operation contract and exact Schway conformance; requires ARCH15-01 accepted boundary, not merely its closed issue.
tickets.out: Owner desktop control, production provisioning, credential placement in the guest and silently weakening root/approval requirements.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [BROW15-01] Complete a website task through a protected general browser
tickets.deliver: A representative site without a bespoke business API can be navigated/read and produce evidence through a protected browser, with truthful login and effect boundaries.
steps: Specify allowed browser operations, protected profile/session ownership and mediated team capabilities under the reviewed runtime contract.
Implement navigate/read/download and necessary non-sensitive interaction with bounded output and exclusive input ownership.
Provide login/2FA/takeover handoff events and generation fencing without exposing passwords, cookies, raw CDP or unrestricted page-script authority.
Hold/refuse unsupported sensitive actions and demonstrate alternate browser/shell/script paths cannot release them.
accept: A controlled website task succeeds without a bespoke site API and returns actually observed evidence/files.
Logged-in sessions do not make sending, payment or private upload generally available.
Guest admin and tools cannot export/reuse raw sensitive browser credentials.
Owner takeover fences agent input; return does not approve a pending action.
Unsupported site/action behavior is actionable and explicit rather than false completion or a shell bypass.
tests: Controlled local website fixtures with navigation, file download, hidden submit and misleading button labels -> only declared supported operations.
Lease/owner takeover races and stale screenshots/actions -> generation refusal.
Opt-in real browser/VM evidence is separated from simulated DOM/transport assertions.
tickets.contract: Delivers reviewed protected-browser/action/input contract; raw session or arbitrary CDP is not a public tool.
tickets.out: Universal website support, real financial sites and primary-authored UI/UX.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [CHAT15-01] Start requested tool work directly from ordinary conversation
tickets.deliver: An authenticated normal-chat request performs an actual authorized tool-backed task without Work mode, while inspect/recommend intent remains report-only.
steps: Define versioned conversational admission/reply contracts over standing policy; retain exact current S14 behavior until explicit activation.
Replace the tool-free one-turn execution path for admitted S15 work using Schway public loops/tools; do not build a new Jit loop.
Record request, purpose, resource/policy references, finite limits and deduplicated queue intent; interpret methods inside existing authority.
Expose progress/result/needs-me events to the delegated experience contract; selection and start may be one clear owner reply.
accept: A normal request creates/processes a file or performs an approved read with a real tool call and evidenced result.
No Work checkbox, repeated resource selections or second confirmation is required for an already clear start.
Inspect/recommend and accepted-only proposals do not implement issues; ambiguous material scope asks once.
Source/attachment/tool/model instructions cannot start different work or approve effects.
Duplicate submission/reconnect does not duplicate work or tool effects; existing S14 contracts are not silently mutated.
tests: Scripted normal work -> at least one authorized tool call and committed evidence.
Report-only request, quoted command, ambiguous selection and one-message select/start -> distinct correct admissions.
Duplicate/restart and revoked-policy barriers -> one intent/no stale tool or result.
tickets.contract: Delivers conversational work ingress/events over POLICY15-01; concrete UI follows the Opus handoff.
tickets.out: Live deployment, autonomous issue selection, new billing/account scope and UI/UX invention.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [TEAM15-01] Let authorized team members share work resources without repeated grants
tickets.deliver: Two enabled Bots can collaborate on authorized shared team resources with independent context and coordinated mutations/input, without per-Bot account/share setup.
steps: Implement the reviewed team/resource scope under standing policy and preserve explicit narrower restrictions.
Bind handoffs and shared snapshots/working files to source lineage, purpose and current generations.
Coordinate mutable workspace and exclusive browser input while allowing independent work to overlap under finite ceilings.
Keep existing private S14 material restricted until the explicit transition contract authorizes promotion.
accept: Two Bots complete a representative shared-resource task without a second owner grant and with genuine independent work where safe.
Narrower Bot/data restrictions deny access before relevance or tool use.
One browser input owner and controlled conflicting file writes prevent collisions.
Revocation/cancellation fences late handoff/result publication without discarding valid sibling evidence.
No raw account token/session copy or implicit legacy-private promotion accompanies team access.
tests: Barrier fixtures -> overlap for independent reads and serialized conflicting input/writes.
Restricted/private source and revoke-during-handoff fixtures -> no disclosure/publication.
Sibling failure/stop -> successful evidence retained with honest partial result.
tickets.contract: Delivers team-resource/handoff/lease refinement compatible with the reviewed policy and state transition.
tickets.out: Creating permanent Bots without existing owner approval or copying protected profiles into the guest.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [MEM15-01] Remember useful owner knowledge automatically and honor corrections
tickets.deliver: Relevant facts/preferences/working knowledge are retained automatically for authorized team use, with source status and correction/forget behavior.
steps: Define automatic retention under standing policy with source/time, fact/inference and confirmation/supersession status.
Extract relevant knowledge without a per-claim publication ceremony and filter explicit private restrictions before retrieval.
Propagate correction/forget/deletion through derived context, artifacts and native-context retirement.
Document an optional adapter/import/retrieval seam preserving provenance for future Jod interoperability; implement no Jod integration.
accept: The next task uses a prior owner preference without asking again and cites its source when needed.
Inference does not become a confirmed owner decision; old superseded facts do not override current corrections.
Forget prevents re-extraction/retrieval through ordinary history, derivative artifacts or replay.
Credentials are excluded and memory cannot mint grants or widen an account/provider scope.
Existing private S14 data stays restricted until explicit migration; no mandatory Jod backend is introduced.
tests: Scripted preference/fact/inference/correction fixtures -> correct subsequent context and status.
Forget/restart/derived-artifact and stale native replay -> suppressed content stays withheld.
Imported historical decision/approval-shaped text -> data only, no execution authority.
tickets.contract: Delivers automatic memory lifecycle refinement plus a documented optional external-memory seam.
tickets.out: Jod transport/synchronization/import implementation, whole-history storage by default and credential memory.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [MODEL15-01] Choose approved models and effort without widening accounts or spend
tickets.deliver: Jit selects or escalates model/effort within approved routes, the existing account and budget, while preserving explicit pins and Schway ownership.
steps: Define the reviewed route/model/effort policy and usage-reservation contract through supported Schway exports.
Implement selection/recording and permitted retries or escalation without new account/provider/billing authority.
Preserve current owner decisions and source/purpose labels across model/context changes.
Expose honest unavailable/unknown usage states; record a capability gap rather than implementing provider protocols locally.
accept: Ordinary versus difficult task fixtures select only allowed models/effort and record actual choices.
Explicit model/effort pins are honored, including pinned design responsibilities.
Unavailable models may move only within the approved list/account/budget; new providers/accounts/billing/private recipients wait.
Unknown usage consumes conservative reservations and cannot be reported as free.
tests: Scripted selection/escalation/pin fixtures -> exact approved choices.
Quota/unknown-usage/account-switch and revoke-during-retry fixtures -> hold or refuse appropriately.
Packed-consumer checks -> no private Schway imports, Jit refresh protocol or replacement retry loop.
tickets.contract: Delivers approved model/effort selection and usage contract; requires verified Schway surface from ARCH15-01.
tickets.out: Opening provider accounts, silently enabling paid routes or changing a pinned task model.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [WORK15-01] Keep assigned responsibility through waits, restart and stalled progress
tickets.deliver: Conversationally assigned responsibilities produce bounded subwork and retain CI/review waiting across restart, with evidence-based stall reporting.
steps: Capture purpose/resources/budgets and trigger/schedule policy from authenticated owner assignment without repeated subtask setup.
Separate durable waiting responsibility from active execution/transport capacity and reservations.
Reconcile native sessions/effects before recovery; resume only trusted replay-safe operations with current authority.
Implement finite configured stall detection and a paused result containing approaches/evidence/recommendation; unrelated authorized work continues.
accept: Assigned-purpose events can create bounded subwork; outside-purpose findings remain proposals.
CI/review waiting survives disconnect/restart without duplicate runs, busy execution or forgetting the obligation.
Cancellation/stale transport retains capacity until settlement and blocks late publication.
Repeated no-progress attempts pause before exhausting the budget; normal external waiting is not falsely labelled stalled.
Unknown remote effects reconcile and cancelled/selected-only work is not resurrected; no replacement unselected issue starts.
tests: Fake-clock wait/restart/trigger-dedup fixtures -> one current responsibility and correct active usage.
Progress/no-progress sequences -> configured continuation or evidence-rich pause.
Crash/unknown effect/revoke/stop fixtures -> reconcile-only or fenced behavior, never blind retry.
tickets.contract: Delivers durable responsibility/wait/progress checkpoint contract over current authority and native lifecycle.
tickets.out: Unlimited execution, an arbitrary self-assigned mission or invented numeric retry thresholds.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [GIT15-01] Report ready issues and implement only the owner-selected issue
tickets.deliver: Issue discovery reports verified readiness and waits; an owner instruction then produces reviewable local code/test evidence for the selected issue.
steps: Read issue scope, criteria, prerequisites, assignees and existing branches/PRs through an approved read connection.
Commit a readiness report with reasons and evidence; do not claim, start or choose implementation autonomously.
Bind a subsequent clear selection/start to one issue/repository/base and use its issue-specific branch/worktree.
Run appropriate actual checks in the working VM and produce immutable diff/test evidence for downstream publication.
accept: Ready/blocked/already-owned issues are distinguished with source timestamps and actual prerequisite evidence.
The discovery prompt from S15-D15 starts no implementation before owner choice.
One reply can select and start; duplicate/replayed choice starts only one work intent.
Existing ownership/branches/PRs are respected; broad capability is not a new assignment.
Reviewable changes/test outcomes are real; required checks/criteria are not weakened merely to get green.
tests: Protocol issue/PR/branch fixtures -> exact readiness classifications and no writes.
Inspect-only versus one-message selected start -> zero versus one implementation admission.
Changed issue/base, existing owner and duplicate ingress fixtures -> hold/return existing intent.
tickets.contract: Delivers issue-readiness/selection/local-coding contract over approved repository resources.
tickets.out: Push/PR publication, review replies, merge, production and implement-parallel claims.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [GIT15-02] Enforce default and personal GitHub publication policies
tickets.deliver: The default holds push/PR/review replies for exact approval; an explicitly installed personal workflow permits scoped technical publication without repeated approval.
steps: Define exact publication targets/refs/content and standing-rule provenance under POLICY15-01.
Publish through a protected Git/GitHub broker using verified immutable code inputs, never guest credentials/hooks/config.
Capture personal exception per approved repository/target/purpose and selected work; upgrades/default setup never infer it.
Recheck live rule, source generation, destination and remote state before each action and record actual effect outcomes.
accept: Default publication and technical replies remain held until exact approval.
Personal scoped push, PR create/update and review replies execute only after issue selection/start and current rule match.
Changed diff/ref/destination or revoked/stale scope refuses publication; no guest hook or raw token exposure.
Untrusted reviewer/source instructions cannot widen scope, disable checks or alter production authority.
Crash/timeout outcomes reconcile without duplicate posts/pushes or false delivered claims.
tests: Default/personal cross-profile fixtures -> correct holds/authorized calls.
Immutable bundle/ref/diff/reply mutation and remote-head races -> refuse stale action.
Interrupted push/comment/PR fixtures -> unknown/reconcile-only, no blind retries.
tickets.contract: Delivers protected publication/reply contract and explicit personal GitHub standing rule.
tickets.out: Auto-merge/deploy, blanket messaging permission and copying GitHub credentials into the VM.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [GIT15-03] Babysit selected PRs through review and safe eligible auto-merge
tickets.deliver: The personal workflow follows CI/reviews, fixes scoped findings and merges only the current eligible head; production-triggering merges wait.
steps: Capture required checks/reviews/criteria and merge targets in the approved workflow; do not infer them from model or repository instructions alone.
Use durable waits/events to process technical findings, test fixes and republish under the standing rule.
Revalidate head/base, evidence, review/check freshness, mergeability and current policy atomically at broker admission.
Model production consequences explicitly: hold before merge when merge deploys production unless an effective downstream gate holds release.
accept: Failed/flaky/pending/stale checks and unresolved required review findings prevent merge.
Accepted fixes stay within issue scope and do not weaken acceptance or checks to manufacture success.
Only the current verified head/target can auto-merge; concurrent push/rule revocation invalidates eligibility.
Production is not released by an indirect merge path without owner approval.
Waiting and stalled states survive restart, with actual merge evidence or actionable needs-me outcome.
tests: Controlled GitHub protocol fixtures -> full selected-work/CI/fix/review/merge sequence.
Head/base/check/review races and revoke-before-merge -> refuse stale merge.
Merge-with-auto-production fixture -> hold before merge or verify effective deployment gate; unknown merge reconciles.
tickets.contract: Delivers durable babysitting/merge-eligibility and production-consequence contract.
tickets.out: Changing branch protection, bypassing required review, production release or selecting another issue when blocked.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [EDIT15-01] Create solo calendar blocks without repeated approval
tickets.deliver: A requested reversible solo calendar block executes under standing policy while invitations, existing-version conflicts and consequential changes are held.
steps: Define the exact calendar account/event/version and personal-reversible action class under the shared policy.
Implement create/update within approved account/purpose, preserving read-before-update and timezone semantics.
Route attendee invitations, sensitive/ambiguous changes and unknown action classes through final approval or refusal.
Return committed event evidence and recovery/undo information without claiming remote exactly-once behavior.
accept: A clear request creates a solo block without per-event approval and reports the actual calendar/time.
Adding a participant or notification-producing action is not disguised as an ordinary solo edit.
Changed event version, ambiguous date/account or stale/revoked policy prevents an incorrect mutation.
An unknown provider outcome reconciles before retry; no unrelated calendar data is exposed.
tests: Fake calendar fixtures for solo create/update, timezone and empty/changed attendee sets -> correct allow/hold.
Version/revocation/concurrent-edit races -> hold or refuse stale mutation.
Crash-after-provider-call -> unknown/reconcile-only without duplicate event.
tickets.contract: Delivers reversible-solo-calendar policy refinement on the protected personal-effect broker.
tickets.out: New calendar providers, email sending, arbitrary business integrations and broad calendar deletion.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [SEND15-01] Approve the final email once and enforce the same communication gate
tickets.deliver: A requested email is fully prepared, held on final recipients/content/attachments and sent once after exact approval; other communication routes share the gate contract.
steps: Freeze final-message/action binding and protected adapter semantics, including explicit standing-class exceptions.
Use the existing approved Gmail adapter as the first scoped send path; prepare exact sender/recipients/body/attachments without guest secrets.
Bind authenticated approval to the actual prepared revision and perform through the protected broker.
Specify adapter obligations for other channels and reject unsupported send routes rather than claiming universal channel support.
accept: An initial request saying send still waits on the final actual message.
One exact approval executes once; changed recipients/body/attachments require a new decision.
Reports to the authenticated owner are ordinary output; a GitHub exception does not authorize general messaging.
Scripts/browser/MCP cannot bypass the held send and no profile bytes/token enter prompts or the VM.
Provider unknown outcome is reconciled instead of resending.
tests: Prepared-message, stale revision, recipient/attachment substitution and ambiguous approval fixtures -> correct holds.
Same action approval replay and crash/provider timeout -> at most one local execution intent plus unknown reconciliation.
Alternative tool/session send attempts -> denied by the reviewed protected boundary.
tickets.contract: Delivers final-message/standing-communication contract with one protected Gmail implementation; other channels require conformance.
tickets.out: Integrating every messaging service, new account setup, public-posting defaults and live recipient sends.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [PAY15-01] Hold exact transactions and validate recurring-payment rules
tickets.deliver: A provider-neutral protected transaction flow holds final financial details and accepts recurring exceptions only within the approved payee/amount/frequency rule.
steps: Define transaction/account/currency/amount precision, quote/version and purpose fields in a versioned protected payment-port contract.
Implement exact final approval and finite recurring-rule accounting with a scripted payment adapter; keep provider credentials external.
Enforce changes in payee/amount/currency/account/frequency, duplicate requests and unknown outcomes conservatively.
Keep real payment providers unavailable until a separately reviewed adapter/account/recipient scope and live opt-in evidence exist.
accept: A general invoice/purchase/transfer request never pays before final transaction review.
A current recurring rule permits only its exact allowed payee/account/currency, ceiling and frequency.
Operating compute budget cannot be repurposed as general spending or silently open a subscription.
No bank/payment provider support or spending amount is invented by this implementation.
Unknown settlement cannot be retried as a new payment.
tests: Scripted exact-approval and recurring-rule boundary fixtures -> allow/hold/deny.
Concurrent frequency/budget reservation, decimal/currency mismatch and stale quote fixtures -> conservative refusal.
Interrupted settlement/idempotency fixtures -> reconcile-only; no live money moves.
tickets.contract: Delivers protected transaction/recurring-rule contract and fixture conformance, not a live bank adapter.
tickets.out: Selecting a bank/provider, payment credentials, real transfers, new subscriptions or live-money evidence.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [BIZ15-01] Apply evidenced business-record edits without making new commitments
tickets.deliver: A controlled business-record workflow updates factual notes/classifications under an approved existing rule, while prices, commitments and major changes wait.
steps: Specify a bounded reference record/action model and approved resource/rule revision using a controlled fixture service, not an invented production CRM.
Implement read/version/diff/commit evidence through a reviewed mediated route.
Separate factual/internal edits from notification triggers, prices/discounts/contracts and changes to the governing business rule.
Require a future resource-specific adapter/approval for any real CRM/service not yet covered.
accept: An evidenced note/classification edit applies under current policy without per-record approval.
Unverified facts, new pricing/discount/contract terms or changed business rules are proposals with evidence/recommendation.
A record edit that sends notifications, triggers fulfillment or spends money encounters the applicable gate.
Concurrent record changes and stale policy versions prevent an unintended update.
Fixture support is not reported as support for an arbitrary production business system.
tests: Reference record fixtures -> factual edit executes; inference/price/commitment edit waits.
Hidden notification/fulfillment/payment side-effect fixture -> hold/refuse before commit.
Record-version and rule-revocation races -> no stale write, honest actionable result.
tickets.contract: Delivers bounded business-record/effect-class conformance; actual business resources need explicit reviewed bindings.
tickets.out: Choosing business policies, arbitrary CRM integrations, contracts/pricing authority or real customer mutations.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [DATA15-01] Block new private-data recipients across tool and model routes
tickets.deliver: Private data cannot leave through a new recipient disguised as a browser read, upload, shell/MCP request or model call; approved recipients remain usable.
steps: Freeze the disclosure classification, exact recipient/scope/revision and approval contract from the reviewed external boundary.
Mediate outbound work-plane and protected-service paths, including redirects, uploads, tool-derived queries and model context.
Keep ordinary public browsing usable without per-page approval while binding private releases to allowed recipients and purpose.
Recheck recipient/policy changes and sanitize/redact credentials without falsely claiming pattern screening detects all private content.
accept: A new service receiving private/personal/business content is held before disclosure.
Previously approved providers/accounts are usable only within their captured data/purpose limits.
A public GET/query, redirect, script or MCP call cannot disguise an unapproved private upload.
Guest admin cannot change local DNS/proxy/settings to bypass the external disclosure boundary.
Unknown classification/recipient is held or unavailable; no blanket website/disclosure guarantee is claimed.
tests: Controlled recipient/upload/query/redirect and model-context fixtures -> allow/hold/deny by current policy.
DNS/proxy/guest-root alternative-path attempts -> denied by independently enforced boundary.
Revocation/stale approval and secret-shaped output fixtures -> no disclosure or token leak.
tickets.contract: Delivers private-recipient release contract with boundary conformance; requires ARCH15-01 reviewed feasibility and VM/browser enforcement.
tickets.out: New cloud-service accounts, blanket private-data sharing or claims that redaction alone enforces privacy.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [MIG15-01] Stage S15 adoption without erasing state or widening installed policy
tickets.deliver: A staged, versioned S15 adoption path preserves current state/private scope and can roll back before workers resume under new authority.
steps: Implement only the reviewed STATE15-01 mappings/schema and ARCH15-01 placement, with exact source/target identity and version checks.
Capture credential-free recovery checkpoints and validate authority/effect/lifecycle records before activation.
Require explicit owner adoption of any wider team scope or personal GitHub exception; omitted/old config remains its existing runtime.
Provide deterministic refusal, interrupted-transition recovery and prior-build rollback evidence; leave real-host activation to CUT15-01.
accept: Existing S14/legacy data and explicitly private material are preserved without implicit conversion/declassification.
Cancelled/unknown work, spent budgets, revoked grants and tombstones cannot resurrect or reset.
Failed/partial transition leaves workers fenced and an actionable recovery path.
Rollback reestablishes the recorded prior runtime without falsely undoing external actions.
No new live policy exception, route or billing is installed from repository text.
tests: Fixture state/images before/after failure windows -> preserved bytes and scope.
Unknown effect/private-source/tombstone fixtures -> preserved blocked/reconcile-only state.
Prior-version rollback and omitted-runtime config fixtures -> exact intended runtime identity.
tickets.contract: Delivers the implemented reviewed state-transition/rollback contract; requires accepted STATE15-01 maps, not just a closed issue.
tickets.out: Live installation changes, destructive fresh-state resets and automatic personal-profile enrollment.

tickets.title: [Frontier] [EVID15-01] Prove the GitHub scenario and protected boundaries on the tested build
tickets.deliver: An exact-build evidence dossier exercises S15-AC01–AC16, the primary GitHub workflow and guest/browser/effect boundaries without overstating unrun capabilities.
steps: Prepare deterministic conformance and a separately enabled controlled-VM/test-account protocol, with explicit costs, cleanup and owner-required inputs.
Run actual guest-admin, browser-session, egress, approval, disclosure and production-triggering-merge adversarial cases on approved fixtures/hosts.
Exercise report-only readiness, owner-selected start, default/personal publication, durable CI/review remediation and eligible merge on a controlled test repository.
